definitions.explanation: effort that yields no result or benefit; work done in vain

examples.japanese: {結局|けっきょく}{骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}だった。
examples.english: In the end, it was all wasted effort.

examples.japanese: {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}に{終|お}わった。
examples.english: It ended up being a waste of effort.

examples.japanese: {準備|じゅんび}したのに{骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}になった。
examples.english: Despite my preparations, it was all for nothing.

notes:
{骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん} describes effort that produces no reward.

WORD FORMATION:
- {骨折|ほねお}り (great effort, pains - literally "bone-breaking")
- {損|ぞん} (loss, damage)

FULL PROVERB:
「{骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}の{くたびれ儲|もう}け」
(All that effort for nothing but exhaustion)
- A proverb meaning hard work that only results in tiredness, with no gain.

USAGE:
- {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}になる (to end up being wasted effort)
- {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}に{終|お}わる (to end in vain)
- {骨折|ほねお}り{損|ぞん}だった (it was a waste of effort)

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {無駄|むだ}{骨|ぼね} (wasted effort)
- {徒労|とろう} (futile effort)
- {水|みず}の{泡|あわ} (come to nothing)
